passage:
Dear Madhuri,
Sorry this is a letter, but I can't say it in the corridor. Today Kabir and a few others kept guessing who writes the poems in the class notebook. They teased me, "Come on, Vandana, you know!" One even hid my geometry box until I answered. I said nothing, and it felt good and awful at once. Your secret is yours to tell. But I want to ask: does hiding it bother you? You look happy when you write, yet you flinch when anyone reads a poem aloud. If you ever want to share them, I'll sit beside you. If not, my lips stay shut. 🙂
Your friend,
Vandana

qa.q: What did one classmate hide until Vandana answered?
qa.a: One classmate hid Vandana's geometry box until Vandana answered.

qa.q: What does Vandana think about the secret, and what worry sits beside that loyalty?
qa.a: Vandana thinks the secret is Madhuri's to tell, but wonders whether hiding it bothers Madhuri, since Madhuri flinches when a poem is read aloud.

qa.q: What could Vandana do next to check the secret is not hurting Madhuri?
qa.a: Ask Madhuri privately how it feels, and offer to sit beside Madhuri if Madhuri ever wants to share the poems. 😊

qa.q: How might Madhuri feel on reading this letter?
qa.a: Probably relieved that Vandana stayed loyal, and maybe a little exposed at being asked; the flinch at hearing a poem aloud shows the secret still matters.

grounding: Vandana keeps a friend's harmless secret through teasing and checks in that it is not weighing on the friend.
